questions.q: Why is Business Rule 1 (auto-assign group by category) configured as Before insert rather than After insert?
options: It makes no functional difference which timing is chosen
Setting current.assignment_group in a Before rule folds the change into the record's single insert write, avoiding a second save
After rules cannot read the current.category field at all
Before rules run only on update, never on insert
questions.explain: Before rules run ahead of the write, so field changes to current are included automatically — exactly what an insert-time default needs, with no extra update() call.

questions.q: In this script, why does the rule check current.operation() even though its own checkboxes already restrict it to insert?
options: To make the rule's intent explicit and keep it safe if the checkboxes are ever reconfigured later
Because without it, the script would run on delete operations instead
To determine the rule's order value automatically
Because current.operation() is required syntax for every Business Rule
questions.explain: The checkbox already scopes this to insert, but the explicit check documents intent and protects the logic if someone later enables update on the same rule.

questions.q: What does the condition `current.priority == 1 && previous.priority != 1` correctly detect in Business Rule 2?
options: That the rule is running in Before timing instead of After
That the incident's assignment_group was just changed
The exact moment an incident escalates to Critical, not every later save of an already-Critical incident
That the incident was just created for the first time
questions.explain: Comparing current to previous isolates the actual transition into Critical — current alone could never distinguish a fresh escalation from an unrelated save.

questions.q: Why must Business Rule 2 be set to run After, rather than Before, update?
options: gs.eventQueue() only works inside Before rules
Before rules cannot read the current.priority field
It looks up and acts on a separate sys_user record (the manager), which is safe to do once the triggering incident's save is already committed
After rules are the only timing that can access the previous object
questions.explain: After is the right timing specifically because the rule's job is touching other, related data (sys_user) — safe only once the incident's own write has already succeeded.

questions.q: What does the Filter Condition on priority changes accomplish for Business Rule 2?
options: It has no real effect since the if-check inside the script already filters correctly
It forces the rule to also run on insert operations
It replaces the need for the previous.priority != 1 comparison entirely
It prevents the rule's script body from running at all for saves that don't touch priority, avoiding wasted server checks
questions.explain: A Filter Condition scopes when the rule executes at all — without one, the script's internal if-logic still runs (and wastes resources) on every unrelated field edit too.
